question.leadin: This ruler bore Caesarion while serving as Julius Caesar's mistress.
question.text: Who is this female Egyptian pharaoh from the Ptolemy dynasty who notably killed herself with a snakebite?
question.clue: This ruler allegedly won a bet by drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar, and while besieged by enemies, this monarch asked for and received a basket of figs.

swap.leadin: Two Hittite spies were tortured in the prelude to this battle, and one side in this battle was commanded by Muwatallis II.
swap.text: Name this 1274 BCE battle in which the Ra and Ptah divisions contributed to the largest chariot battle in history.
swap.clue: In this battle, the Ra and Amun divisions were initially routed by attacks across the Orontes River launched by Muwatalli II.

question.leadin: The Greeks referred to this man as Ozymandias.
question.text: Name this "great" Egyptian pharaoh who defeated the Nile "Sea People" and claimed a victory at the 1274 BCE Battle of Kadesh.
question.clue: His refusal to extradite the deposed king Mursili III to Hattusili III led to the signing of the world's first peace treaty.

swap.text: The discovery of this pharaoh's tomb was monumental because it was nearly fully intact, with very few artifacts stolen by grave robbers. Howard Carter discovered the tomb of this pharaoh, the youngest ruler of Egypt.
swap.clue: One of this ruler's names which invoked the god Aten was changed after his "Restoration" reversed his probable father's monotheism.

question.text: This pharaoh of the Old Kingdom is most famous for ordering his architect Hemon to begin the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
question.clue: Flinders Petrie discovered the only three-dimensional depiction of this ruler, a small ivory statuette.

swap.leadin: The first one of these entities was built by Djoser, but more famous ones can be found at Giza.
swap.text: Name these structures often built as tombs for Pharaohs, such as ones for Khafre and Menkaure. The Great Sphinx is located in front of several of them.
swap.clue: A switch from a 54 degree inclination to a 43 degree inclination gives the "Bent" one its name.

question.leadin: This city's "Supremacy" over Greece lasted for much of the early 4th century BC.
question.text: Name this central Greek city whose elite troops, the Sacred Band, consisted of 150 pairs of male lovers. It was legendarily the home of King Oedipus and was founded by Cadmus.
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Old Kingdom pharaohs.
swap.text: Name this pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.
swap.clue: This founder of the First Dynasty depicted on a namesake "Palette" who unified Upper and Lower Egypt.

question.text: The Story of Sinuhe ("sin-NOO-hay") references the murder of Amenemhat I, a ruler of this Egyptian kingdom that ruled between the first two Intermediate Periods.
question.clue: The fnal rulers of this period were called the Xois Dynasty since they moved the capital there.

swap.text: After an earthquake, the Rhodeans rejected the offer of a ruler of this name to repair the Colossus. A member of the Diadochi with this name stole Alexander the Great's body and interred it in Alexandria.
swap.clue: One ruler of this name won the Battle of Raphia against Antiochus the Great and married his sister, Arsinoe III.

question.leadin: The last inscription in this writing system is the Graffito of Esmet-Akhom in the late 4th Century CE.
question.text: Name this script. Jean-Francois Champollion used the Rosetta Stone to decipher this form of writing, which was included on the stone along with Greek and Demotic.

swap.text: This Alexandrian mathematician wrote a commentary on Diophantus' Arithmetica. This Neoplatonist philosopher and pagan was killed after she advised the governor Orestes in his feud with Patriarch Cyril.
swap.clue: Her only known work is a commentary on Book III of her father, Theon's, edition of Ptolemy's Almagest although she may have worked on his edition of 's Elements as well.

question.text: This group is often credited with introducing chariot warfare to ancient Egypt. This group ruled over the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt from the city of Avaris.
question.clue: In a satirical story, a ruler of these people complains that he can't sleep because of noisy hippos in a letter addressed to Seqenenre ("sek-en-EN-ray") Tao.

swap.leadin: This site's monuments include the tomb of Horemheb, the mastaba of Ti, and the tomb of Ramesses II's treasurer Ptah-M-Wia, whose pink sarcophagus was discovered in 2022.
swap.text: Name this site where Unas was buried with the first Pyramid Texts. This necropolis near Memphis is the site of the earliest known pyramids, including the Buried Pyramid and the Step Pyramid of Djoser designed by Imhotep.
swap.clue: Religious texts were carved on the subterranean walls of structures in this site, including one dedicated to the ruler Unas ("YOO-niss").

question.leadin: Name the following Middle Eastern rulers who made famous steles.
question.text: A stele named for this pharaoh discovered by Flinders Petrie contains the oldest known instance of the word "Israel" and depicts his defeat of the Libyans. This man was the son and successor of Ramses II.

swap.leadin: Name these rulers from the 18th dynasty within the Egyptian New Kingdom.
swap.text: This pharaoh's campaigns included wins over the Mitanni Empire and the Canaanites at Megiddo. He wiped away many images of his female predecessor, Hatshepsut.
swap.answerHtml: Thutmose III [accept Thutmosis III or Tuthmosis III; prompt on “Thutmose”; prompt “Thutmosis”]
swap.clue: This ruler's most famous victory was a seven-month siege of Canaanites.

question.leadin: Answer the following about African queens.
question.text: Reliefs on Queen Hatshepsut's temple at Deir el-Bahri depict the expedition she sent to this foreign land, probably in the Horn of Africa, from which the Egyptians obtained ebony and incense.
question.clue: An expedition to this place led by the Chancellor Nehsi was recorded in inscriptions in the mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahri.

swap.leadin: The second story in this text is about a man who fashions a wax crocodile, which comes to life on contact with water, and eats the man who slept with his wife.
swap.text: Name this ancient document discovered by a namesake British explorer, which consists of five tales about magicians. In another of its stories, the heroine Rededjet gives birth to three future kings, by the prophecy of Dedi.

question.leadin: Name these men involved in the power struggle after the death of Alexander the Great, FTPE.
question.text: He finally put down the ambitious campaigns of Perdiccas and seized the body of Alexander to stake his claim to the empire, though he eventually encouraged the dissolution of the empire and settled for just being King of Egypt.
question.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.

swap.text: This man became the third head librarian of the Library around 240 BCE, and he may be best known for developing a namesake "sieve" that identifies prime numbers.
swap.clue: To accomplish one of his tasks, this man hired a number of bematists to walk 5,000 stadia.
